# MDL101 · `utf8-bom`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

The file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | loading |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | safe |
| Flags | unsuppressible |
| Design references | K15, case 06 |

## Why

GLib does not skip a byte order mark. The first line becomes `\ufeff[mydumper]`, which is neither a group, a key/value pair nor a comment, so GLib rejects the file and mydumper ignores all of it. Editors add a BOM when saving as "UTF-8 with BOM".

## Example

❌ Before:

```text
\ufeff[mydumper]
threads=4

[`app`.`users`]
`email`=random_string

[client]
user=backup
```

(`\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` stand for the bytes they name, `·` for a trailing space)

```text
1:1-1:2 error MDL101[utf8-bom] file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM)
  = mydumper ignores this entire file: it only logs a WARNING ("Failed to load config file") and runs with its defaults. The MySQL client library rejects the file too ("Found option without preceding group"), so the [client] settings are lost: without connection options on the command line mydumper cannot connect; with them it runs, exit code 0. The masking rules are NOT applied: masked columns are dumped in plaintext.
  fix (safe): Remove the byte order mark
```

✅ After `mydumper-lint check --fix`:

```ini
[mydumper]
threads=4

[`app`.`users`]
`email`=random_string

[client]
user=backup
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL101: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
